practices_evaluation.practice_title: Responsible Addition of Test Code Maintenance
practices_evaluation.justification: The test interacts only with public API (constructor and numVertices) and does not use reflection or access private fields. It verifies observable behavior rather than implementation details.

The test uses a specific assertion method (assertEquals) and includes a descriptive failure message. The single assertion includes a message, which satisfies the requirement that assertions be specific and descriptive.
The method includes minimal, helpful Given/When/Then comments that explain the test's intent (why), and there is no commented-out code. Comments add value without cluttering implementation details.

The test contains no sources of non-determinism (no Random, no System.currentTimeMillis(), no Thread.sleep()). It depends only on deterministic construction and method call, so results are repeatable.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Complete Avoidance of Test Side Effects

PRINCIPLE: Each test should focus on a single requirement/behavior with one Arrange-Act-Assert. RATIONALE: Single-focus tests make failures easy to diagnose. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Look for multiple distinct 'Act' method calls or multiple Assert groups. DECISION RULES: (1) Count distinct Act operations; (2) Check test name for multiple operations; (3) If a single method call tested and single assertion group then compliant. ANALYSIS & DECISION: The test performs setup (insereAresta) and then calls retiraAresta as the action under test and asserts expected outcomes. The intent is to test the behavior of retiraAresta when removing a non-existent edge; insereAresta is setup, not a second Act under test. There is one clear act under test and a single group of assertions about that act. VERDICT: compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Tests must not depend on other tests; use setup/teardown to isolate. RATIONALE: Independence allows tests to run in any order. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Check for @Before/@After or shared mutable state. DECISION RULES: (1) Look for setup/teardown annotations; (2) Check for static/instance vars used by tests; (3) If only local variables are used mark compliant. ANALYSIS & DECISION: The method uses only local variables and constructs a fresh Grafo instance; there is no evidence of shared mutable state or test-order naming. Although no @Before/@After is present, the absence of shared mutable state and the use of local variables satisfy independence. VERDICT: compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Coverage of Normal and Exceptional Flows
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: For each method under test there should be tests for both happy and error paths. RATIONALE: Ensures robustness across valid and invalid inputs. EVALUATION CRITERIA: There should be at least two tests per behavior: one happy path and one error case (or use of assertThrows/@Test(expected=...)). DECISION RULES: (1) If all tests only use valid inputs mark non-compliant; (2) Look for @Test(expected=...) or assertThrows; (3) Check test names for 'invalid', 'null', etc.; (4) If class has < 2 tests total likely non-compliant. ANALYSIS & DECISION: This test exercises an error condition (removing a non-existing edge) but the class contains only this single test method; there is no corresponding happy-path test in the provided snippet that verifies successful removal behavior for the same operation. The evaluation rules require at least a happy and an error test per method under test. Therefore this single-method class does not satisfy the requirement. VERDICT: non-compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should validate minimum, maximum, and just-outside boundaries. RATIONALE: Boundaries are common sources of bugs. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Look for explicit boundary values (0, -1, Integer.MAX_VALUE, empty strings) or names indicating edges. DECISION RULES: (1) Presence of boundary test data indicates compliance; (2) Names may indicate boundaries; (3) If all data are middle-range values mark non-compliant; (4) If method has no boundaries mark not-applicable. ANALYSIS & DECISION: The test uses V=313 and calls indices 0 and 1; it does not exercise boundary indices like V-1 or invalid indices (e.g., -1 or V). There is no explicit boundary-value coverage. Therefore it fails to satisfy boundary-value analysis. VERDICT: non-compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should be self-contained and reuse helpers for repeated logic. RATIONALE: Reduces duplication and improves readability. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Look for helper methods, constants, or duplication across tests. DECISION RULES: (1) Presence of helpers and constants => compliant; (2) Repeated blocks across tests => non-compliant; (3) Very short tests (<10 lines) with no repeat => compliant. ANALYSIS & DECISION: The method is short and self-contained; there is no repeated code shown across multiple tests (only one test provided). While there are no helper methods or constants, the brevity and lack of duplication lead to compliant under the provided rules. VERDICT: compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Detailed Analysis of Size and Complexity
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Keep tests small and avoid complex control flow. RATIONALE: Low complexity reduces the chance of bugs in tests. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Tests <20 lines and no loops/nested conditionals are compliant. DECISION RULES: (1) If any method >30 lines mark non-compliant; (2) If loops/complex conditionals present mark non-compliant; (3) If methods <15 lines and simple, mark compliant. ANALYSIS & DECISION: The test is short (<20 lines) contains no loops or conditional logic and follows linear Arrange-Act-Assert flow. VERDICT: compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Assertions should verify multiple relevant properties. RATIONALE: More comprehensive assertions detect deeper faults. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Verify multiple properties of results or collection size+contents. DECISION RULES: (1) If only one superficial assertion mark non-compliant; (2) If tests verify >=2 properties mark compliant. ANALYSIS & DECISION: The test asserts both that retiraAresta returned null and that the graph vertex count remained 313 — two related properties verifying behavior and state. These multiple assertions improve fault detection. VERDICT: compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Avoid ignored or commented-out tests; keep tests runnable. RATIONALE: Ignored tests hide issues. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Search for @Ignore/@Disabled or commented-out @Test methods. DECISION RULES: (1) If @Ignore/@Disabled present mark non-compliant; (2) If commented-out tests present mark non-compliant; (3) Otherwise compliant. ANALYSIS & DECISION: There is no @Ignore/@Disabled or commented-out test methods in the provided method. The test is active and runnable. VERDICT: compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Tests should be traceable to requirements. RATIONALE: Traceability aids impact analysis. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Presence of annotations or Javadoc referencing requirement IDs. DECISION RULES: (1) Search for @Story/@Requirement/@Issue etc.; (2) Search for REQ-/US-/JIRA- in Javadoc; (3) If none present mark non-compliant. ANALYSIS & DECISION: The class-level Javadoc includes 'Traceability: REQ-GRAFO-SMOKE', which explicitly links tests to a requirement. That satisfies the traceability criterion even though it's at class level rather than method level. VERDICT: compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Rigorous Use of Performance and Security Tests
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Performance/security testing should be explicit and separate. RATIONALE: Non-functional requirements need dedicated tests. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Look for explicit performance tests (@Test(timeout=...)) or security checks. DECISION RULES: (1) Usually not-applicable for unit tests; (2) Mark compliant ONLY if explicit performance/security tests are present; (3) Mark non-compliant only if class name suggests such tests. ANALYSIS & DECISION: The test method is annotated with @Test(timeout = 4000), an explicit timeout indicating a performance constraint is being enforced by the test runner. Under the decision rules this counts as an explicit performance-related assertion, so mark compliant. VERDICT: compliant.

PRINCIPLE: Test names should clearly describe scenario and expected outcome. RATIONALE: Descriptive names are self-documenting. EVALUATION CRITERIA: Names should follow patterns like methodName_scenario_expectedResult. DECISION RULES: (1) If name follows pattern mark compliant; (2) If generic names like test1/test6 mark non-compliant. ANALYSIS & DECISION: The method is named 'test6', an auto-generated generic name that does not describe the scenario or expected result. Despite class-level Javadoc describing intent, the method name itself fails the clear-naming criterion. VERDICT: non-compliant.

practices_evaluation.practice_title: Small Footprint of Test Code Generation
practices_evaluation.justification: PRINCIPLE: Avoid heavy auto-generated verbose tests and names. RATIONALE: Generated tests can be verbose and less maintainable.
